records.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza's fictionalised modern hybrid Formula car, the Gen2 of the Formula Ultimate line. No real-world chassis identity is assigned. It is a separate car from Formula Ultimate Hybrid Gen3, which AMS2 places in its own class family.
records.confidence_basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and all three of the car's aero identities were observed in live telemetry.
records.identity_basis: The identity is Reiza's own model name, observed exactly in live telemetry in all three of its aero configurations; no real-world chassis identity is assigned.
records.specification_basis: The live drive selected eight paddle gears with automatic cut and blip and no clutch needed to pull away, which is the modern hybrid Formula pattern the class represents.
records.confidence_notes: Guided testing directly established the eight paddle gears, the clutch-free move-off, the clutchless running shifts, and automatic cut and blip.
control_notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts, automatic blip on downshifts, and no clutch needed to pull away, so the driver supplies none of the three.
Eight forward gears, matching the modern Formula One hybrid era the class represents and the other Formula Ultimate records.

This is a different car from Formula Ultimate Hybrid Gen3. AMS2 places Gen2 in the F-Ultimate class family and Gen3 in F-Ultimate_Gen2, so the class numbering is offset from the car numbering by one. Nothing is inherited between them.

additional_telemetry_names.basis: Base configuration of the same car, observed exactly in live telemetry in the F-Ultimate class. AMS2 selects the aero configuration from the circuit, so a driver reaches this identity without choosing it. Controls are inherited from the driven high-downforce configuration and were not separately tested.
